::: {#def-deviance}

#### Deviance

The **deviance** of a fitted logistic regression with labels $\outvar_\iobs \in \set{0, 1}$ is minus twice its maximized log-likelihood:

$$
\deviance \eqdef -2 \, \llikf{\hvcoef}
= -2 \sumin \cb{\outvar_\iobs \ln \hat\prob_i + \paren{1 - \outvar_\iobs} \ln\paren{1 - \hat\prob_i}},
$$ {#eq-deviance}

where $\hat\prob_i = \sigmoidf{\dprod{\hvcoef}{\vpredvar_\iobs}}$ is the fitted probability.

:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" collapse=true}
## Source

@nelder1972generalized introduced the deviance for the whole family of generalized linear models;
logistic regression is the case of Bernoulli outcomes with the logit link.
@hastie2009elements [Section 4.4.2] defines the residual deviance of a fitted logistic regression as minus twice its log-likelihood.
:::
